title: Mechanical Energy
learning_goal: Investigate and calculate kinetic energy and potential energy.

stages.title: 1. Energy of motion and position
stages.content: Mechanical energy includes kinetic energy, the energy of motion, and potential energy, energy stored because of position or configuration.

stages.title: 2. Kinetic energy
stages.content: Kinetic energy is KE = ½mv². It increases with mass and increases strongly with speed because speed is squared.

stages.title: 3. Gravitational potential energy
stages.content: Near Earth's surface, gravitational potential energy is PE = mgh, where h is measured relative to a chosen reference level.

stages.title: 4. Worked example
stages.content: A 2 kg object moves at 4 m/s. Its kinetic energy is KE = ½(2)(4²) = 16 J.

stages.title: 5. Guided practice
stages.prompt: A 3 kg backpack is lifted 2 m above the floor. Using g = 9.8 m/s², what is its gravitational potential energy relative to the floor?
stages.alternate_explanation: Multiply mass by gravitational field strength and height.

stages.title: 6. Mastery check
stages.content: To demonstrate mastery, calculate kinetic and gravitational potential energy, compare how mass, speed, and height affect energy, and identify appropriate reference levels.
